transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Later this hour, the Labor Department will release the latest monthly snapshot of the
jobs picture for the nation.
The agency said that job growth was weak in July but rebounded in August.
Some economic forecasters think between 80,000 and 90,000 new jobs were created in September.
Mark Zandi is the chief economist at Moody's Analytics, and he's reflected on last month's
potential job growth.
"I'm struggling with the right word to describe how I feel about it.
You know, this sounds bland, but it's okay, you know, I'll take it.
It's enough jobs to keep unemployment from rising and unemployment is very low.
But just don't lose your job because no one's hiring.
Hiring rates are about as low as they've ever been, the number of hours people are working
is very low."
He spoke to NPR's Morning Edition.
President Trump is campaigning for Republican candidates in red states ahead of the November
midterms.
President is scheduled to be in Mobile, Alabama today, and Pierre's Danielle Kurtzleben says
Trump made an appearance in yesterday in Durant, Oklahoma.
Trump's speech, which lasted nearly an hour and a half, covered familiar ground, like
promoting Republican tax cuts and baselessly accusing Democrats of cheating in elections.
Saturday he is scheduled to speak in Ohio.
That state, which has turned redder in recent years, has tight Senate and governor's races
this year.
When asked why he's campaigning in solidly Republican states like Oklahoma, he responded,
"I won all of them by a lot.
I'm going there just to make sure."
He added that he wanted to thank Oklahoma for voting for him in three presidential elections.
Danielle Kurtzleben, NPR News.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul is expected to speak this morning about the special investigation
into an alleged rape case at Cornell University.
She'll be joined by New York Attorney General Letitia James.
She's been named as special prosecutor to re-examine this case.
The Trump administration has now cut refugees and other groups of immigrants with legal
status off from Medicaid.
And PR Selena Simmons-Duffin reports the change is a result of Republicans' One Big Beautiful
Bill Act.
Mustafa Rafat has lately been fielding frantic phone calls from refugees with disabilities.
It's a nightmare for the community.
It's a very emotional time because they also lost their access to food stamps.
Rafat is a professor of social work at the University of Nebraska at Omaha and a former
refugee himself.
He points out these are new Americans who are often struggling with complex health issues
while adjusting to a new culture.
Making their health and well-being worse is not going to benefit anyone.
In a statement to NPR, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services emphasized it is implementing
a law passed by Congress.
Selena Simmons-Duffin, NPR News, Washington.
You're listening to NPR.
The Trump administration has restored specialized suicide prevention service for LGBTQ+ youth
through the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline.
The service returned on Wednesday.
NPR's Ritu Chatterjee reports that is more than 14 months after it was suddenly shut
down.
The 988 helpline had received nearly 1.3 million contacts from LGBTQ+ youth over three years
before it was shut down.
Those contacts included calls, texts and online chats.
In January of this year, the U.S. Senate passed a bipartisan bill to fund the Federal Health
Department that also mandated the restoration of the specialized service on 988.
Democratic Senator Tammy Baldwin of Wisconsin is a lead sponsor of that legislation.
I hope the restoration will restore trust and faith that people should indeed reach
out to 988.
LGBTQ+ youth can once again access specialized crisis support tailored for them by dialing
988 and then pressing option 3.
Ritu Chatterjee, NPR News.
A court in Japan has ordered that legal protection be given to the human voice.
This stems from a lawsuit filed by a Japanese anime voice actor.
He had sued a content creator on the online platform TikTok for using cloned imitations
of his voice created by AI.
The judge said the human voice is symbolic of individual personality, just like one's
portrait.
This is NPR.
Stay tuned for the following announcements and messages from our sponsors.

topics.text: Labor Department releases September jobs report showing weaker hiring than expected
President Trump campaigns in Oklahoma and Alabama for Republican candidates ahead of midterms
New York Governor Hochul addresses special investigation into alleged rape case at Cornell University
Trump administration cuts Medicaid coverage for refugees and other legal immigrants
Trump administration restores LGBTQ+ youth suicide prevention service on 988 Lifeline
Japanese court orders legal protection for human voice in AI voice cloning case
